author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both veterinarian directory surfaces accept an optional specialty selection and list only the veterinarians holding it. Matching is on the whole name, ignoring letter case. A blank selection or none narrows nothing; a specialty nobody holds returns an empty directory, not a failure.
acceptance_criteria: Both directory surfaces accept an optional specialty selection, named `specialty`, on the existing routes `/vets.html` and `/vets`.
Given a specialty at least one veterinarian holds, when either surface is narrowed to it, then only veterinarians holding that specialty are listed.
Given a narrowed page surface, when the results exceed one page, then they are listed a page at a time as the unnarrowed directory is.
Given a specialty name differing from the stored name only by letter case, when either surface is narrowed to it, then it matches.
Given only the opening letters of a specialty name, when either surface is narrowed to it, then no veterinarian matches.
Given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either surface is narrowed to it, then the directory is returned with no veterinarians in it and the request succeeds with the normal response.
Given a specialty selection that is empty or made only of spaces, when either surface is requested, then the result matches the same request with no selection at all.
Given no specialty selection, when either surface is requested, then it behaves exactly as it does today.
Given a veterinarian holding several specialties, when the directory is narrowed to any one of them, then that veterinarian is listed.
non_goals: Free-text search over veterinarian names — NG-9 stays in force for that, as narrowed by the 2026-08-05 non-goal ADR
Narrowing the directory by any attribute other than specialty
Any write flow over veterinarians or specialties (NG-2)
Paging the machine-readable directory — it carries every match in one document
notes: REQ-VET-004 (machine-readable directory is a supported surface) is minted in this dispatch but carries no slice of its own: the surface and its test already exist, and this slice adds the only capability asked of it. Two reconciliations fall outside my write scope. (1) docs/system-design.md line 207 still lists 'The machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement ... pending removal' in its known-defects table — stale as of the REQ-VET-004 reinstatement; system-design-expert owns the fix. (2) docs/adr/README.md's Index table needs a row for docs/adr/2026-08-05-non-goal-veterinarian-search.md; the README is not in the product-requirements-expert write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package and adds no type, module, or layer: the filter is two new derived query methods on VetRepository plus an optional request parameter on the two existing VetController routes. Two decisions make it new ground rather than a repeat of the owner-search pattern, and both are now recorded. First, case-insensitivity is folded inside the query rather than delegated to the column type or collation, so the filter matches identically on H2, MySQL, and PostgreSQL (docs/adr/2026-08-05-query-expressed-case-insensitive-matching.md, restated in docs/system-design.md Persistence). Copying the neighbouring owner-search arrangement would reproduce the confirmed PostgreSQL case-sensitivity defect on a second surface, invisibly to the H2-backed suite. Second, the filtered reads carry no caching annotation, because their cache key would be a request-supplied value entering a cache the JCache configuration leaves unbounded (docs/adr/2026-08-05-request-derived-vet-cache-keys.md, restated in docs/system-design.md Contracts). The unfiltered reads keep their cache. Basis for the covering-symbol claims: grep over the vet package and OwnerRepository, no IDE oracle connected.
integration_points: VetRepository gains two reads selecting on the joined Specialty name, case-folded in the query: one paged for /vets.html, one unpaged Collection for /vets. Neither is annotated @Cacheable.

VetController.showVetList and showResourcesVetList each take an optional specialty request parameter and choose between the filtered and unfiltered repository read. The blank-to-absent normalization sits here as request-shape normalization at the HTTP trust boundary, not as a business rule; the matching rule itself lives in the query, so the pattern catalog's no-new-controller-rules bar is not crossed.

vetList.html pagination links currently hardcode /vets.html?page=N and carry no other parameter. Every one of the six links must carry the active specialty forward, or page two of a filtered directory silently reverts to the unfiltered list.
docs/system-design.md Contracts: Vets now implements REQ-VET-004, VetController implements REQ-VET-001/003/004, VetRepository implements REQ-VET-001/003.

patterns.description: the existing derived paged query with a Pageable second argument — follow its shape, but not its delegation of case-folding to the schema
findPaginated builds the PageRequest; the filtered path reuses it and changes only which repository read it calls

risks.risk: A paged query whose predicate traverses the EAGER @ManyToMany specialties association can make Hibernate apply the page in memory if it join-fetches the collection alongside the paged root query.
risks.mitigation: The paging test must seed more matching veterinarians than one page holds and assert the second page's contents, not just its existence. If in-memory paging appears, keep the filter predicate free of a fetch join and let the eager collection load in its own select, as findAll(Pageable) already does.

risks.risk: All VetRepository reads share the one cache name vets, so two methods whose arguments generate the same key would serve an unfiltered list to a filtered request — a wrong answer with no error.
risks.mitigation: The filtered reads stay uncached (ADR 2026-08-05-request-derived-vet-cache-keys), which keeps the cached key space fixed at its current two shapes.

risks.risk: The specialty value is caller-supplied and unauthenticated on an open route.
risks.mitigation: It reaches the database only through a derived, parameterized query — no concatenated query text. If the value is echoed back into the page, it stays in th:text or th:value so Thymeleaf's default escaping applies; th:utext is out.

notes: Reconciliations from the prd-entry notes are applied. (1) The known-defect row saying the machine-readable veterinarian route serves no requirement is removed from docs/system-design.md, and the provenance line's defect count is corrected from four to three; the withdrawal history stays in the PRD's Superseded list, since system-design carries current state only. (2) docs/adr/README.md's Index gained rows for the non-goal ADR and for the two ADRs this triage wrote. Unstated behavior the implementer will hit: the acceptance criteria fix a blank or whitespace-only value as equivalent to absent but say nothing about a padded non-blank value such as ' radiology '. Recommend one normalization rather than two — trim once, treat the empty result as absent, and match on the trimmed value — and note the choice in the test name or a comment so a reviewer reads it as a decision rather than an accident. Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so nothing to audit.

approved_aspects: Cache hazard from the design ADR is correctly closed: both filtered reads (findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, collection and paged) carry no @Cacheable, and a grep of src/main/java confirms @Cacheable("vets") remains only on the two fixed-key-space findAll variants. architectural_fit: Unchanged from the superseded record at line 9; no code, document, or design decision moves. This revision resolves the doc-reviewer clarify finding at line 20 (docs/system-design.md:80) and carries the same design-doc path coverage forward. The finding was correct on the abstraction level and understated the defect: the cache name is not merely an unsourced literal, it is a load-bearing duplicate. The literal now has a Constants row naming CacheConfiguration.java as its source, the row records the unboundedness (statistics-only JCache configuration, no size limit, no expiry) that the Contracts invariant and the cache-keys ADR both depend on, and the invariant sentence points at Constants instead of restating the value. patterns.description: the unique_owner_pet_name Constants row - the project's form for a literal that two source files must agree on: Name column carries the literal, Source column cites the file that owns it, Description states what breaks when the two diverge

risks.risk: The invariant as previously written ('Every VetRepository read shares the one cache name') became false when this slice added two uncached reads, and it contradicted its own next clause. Sourcing the literal without repairing the quantifier would have left a correct pointer attached to a wrong claim.
risks.mitigation: The sentence now scopes the claim to the cached reads, which is what the ADR's consistency argument actually rests on.

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: The Consequences bullet 'All vet reads still share the one cache name, so the cached methods' keys must stay distinguishable by argument shape alone' is factually wrong today, in the same way the pre-fix system-design.md invariant was: the two specialty-filtered VetRepository reads carry no @Cacheable annotation (confirmed by source read) and so do not share the cache at all — the ADR's own Decision section says exactly this ('the specialty-filtered reads carry no caching annotation'). The system-design-expert's stated reason for leaving this unchanged — that an ADR records state at decision time and so the source-rename self-test does not bind it — does not hold here: this ADR was authored within this same slice, not inherited from an earlier decision the world has since moved past, and the sentence was wrong at authoring time, not by later drift. documentation-standards.md's decision-time-voice exemption (line 76) covers grammatical person ('we'/'you'), not factual accuracy of claims. The ADR is Accepted and is the document system-design.md's Contracts invariant links to as authoritative backing for the cache-key rule, so a reader who acts on this ADR without re-deriving the source is misled about which reads participate in the cache. This is the same defect class the round-1 finding at handoff.jsonl line 20 uncovered in system-design.md (an invariant whose quantifier is contradicted by its own neighboring content); a sweep of the other two 2026-08-05 ADRs and system-design.md found no further instances.

approved_aspects: docs/prd.md:138 edge case 3 no longer uses 'several' or any other prohibited word from documentation-standards.md; a full-document grep for the entire prohibited-word list confirms no other instance, resolving the round-1 finding at handoff.jsonl line 20 without loss of meaning

The reworded edge case ('A veterinarian holding more than one specialty is listed when the directory is filtered to any one of those specialties.') states the same behavioral condition as the original phrasing and stays within the PRD's behavioral-language boundary

author: security-reviewer

findings.description: The temporary repoint of the JSON directory at the paged read is NOT reverted. showResourcesVetList still reads `this.vetRepository.findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(requestedSpecialty, PageRequest.of(0, 5)).getContent()` — the two-arg paged overload, capped at five. Three corroborating signals that this is leftover scaffolding rather than intent: (1) it contradicts PRD edge case 2 as reworded in this very change set ('The machine-readable directory carries every matching veterinarian in one document; paging applies to the page surface only'); (2) the new test theMachineReadableVetDirectoryShouldCarryEveryMatchInOneDocument and the round-1 test theMachineReadableVetDirectoryShouldCarryOnlyVeterinariansHoldingTheRequestedSpecialty both stub only the one-arg overload, so against this source the unstubbed paged mock returns null and `.getContent()` throws NPE — the requests 500 and the assertions on status().isOk() fail; (3) the line is 114 characters and unwrapped, which spring-javaformat would not emit, so `checkFormat` would fail too — the working tree was edited after the gate that recorded build-pass at line 26. Consequence if shipped: the machine-readable directory silently truncates a filtered result to five veterinarians with no next-page signal, and the one-arg `findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String)` becomes production-dead code. No security regression is introduced by the leftover itself — the paged filtered read is uncached exactly like the unpaged one — but the gate my round-1 approval rested on no longer describes this tree, so it must be re-run after the revert.
findings.fix: Restore the unpaged read: `this.vetRepository.findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(requestedSpecialty)` in the ternary's else branch, then re-run `./gradlew format` and the full quality gate (build, test, check) before re-review.

approved_aspects: Production code under src/main is byte-identical to the round-1 review tree (`git diff <round-1 tree_sha> -- src/main/` is empty), so no new production surface entered in round 2 — the only defect is the pre-existing un-reverted line above.

The uncached-filtered-read property I approved in round 1 still holds in the source: a sweep of all cache annotations across src/main (`grep -rn 'Cacheable|CachePut|CacheEvict'`) finds @Cacheable on exactly the two whole-list VetRepository reads and on nothing else. Neither findBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase overload is cached, so no request-supplied specialty string is ever promoted to a key in the unbounded `vets` cache.

No SQL injection surface: both filtered reads are Spring Data derived query methods (parameter-bound), and a sweep for @Query / createQuery / createNativeQuery / String.format / concat across src/main finds only one unrelated static JPQL string in PetTypeRepository.

No XSS: the specialty value re-enters the page only through Thymeleaf `@{/vets.html(page=..,specialty=${specialty})}` link expressions, which URL-encode the parameter and HTML-escape the attribute; vetList.html adds no th:utext, inline javascript, or raw-output construct.
No secrets in the change set: sweep of the diff for token/password/secret/key/credential yields nothing; the only new literal is the `vets` cache name, already a public configuration identifier.

Supply chain unchanged: build.gradle and gradle/ are untouched by this change set (`git status --porcelain build.gradle gradle/` is empty), so no new or version-bumped dependency enters and the CVE surface is identical to the last verified state.

The new Constants row for `vets` states the cache's unboundedness accurately. CacheConfiguration builds `new MutableConfiguration<>().setStatisticsEnabled(true)` and nothing else: no ExpiryPolicy is set (JCache defaults to Eternal) and JSR-107 carries no size configuration at all, which the class's own javadoc says must come from the provider's mechanism. No such mechanism exists here — the provider is Caffeine's JCache adapter (build.gradle runtimeOnly) and there is no ehcache.xml, caffeine spec, or spring.cache.* property anywhere under src/main/resources. 'statistics alone with no size limit and no expiry' is therefore literally what the code does, and 'unbounded' follows.

The repaired Contracts invariant is now true where the old one was false. It scopes the quantifier to 'the VetRepository reads that are cached', which matches the two @Cacheable reads and excludes the two filtered ones, and it restates the reason the filtered reads stay uncached (a request-supplied value in the key of an unbounded cache) with a link to the governing ADR. The falsified universal claim is gone.
